title: Spin-incoherent Mott-Thouless pumps
authors: Ajesh Kumar, Urban F. P. Seifert, Erez Berg, Achim Rosch
abstract: A Thouless pump describes a system in which a quantized amount of charge is transported by one lattice spacing per cycle when the parameters of a Hamiltonian are varied slowly and periodically. In the standard case, this quantization requires the system to remain in its ground state with vanishing thermodynamic entropy throughout the pumping process. Here, we introduce a class of Mott-Thouless pumps, which operate in highly entropic, spin-incoherent Mott states. We show analytically that these states exhibit exponentially protected quantized transport despite their extensive entropy, because the pumped charge resides in a gapped sector that remains dynamically decoupled from the hot spin degrees of freedom. By contrast, motivated by a recent experimental realization, we identify other classes of Mott-Thouless pumps that lack this protection. In these systems, spin excitations can efficiently generate charge excitations, leading to a rapid breakdown of quantized transport. Our analytical results are supported by numerically exact real-time simulations of finite systems.
summary: This paper analyzes Mott-Thouless pumps, extending the concept of quantized charge transport to highly entropic, spin-incoherent Mott states. The authors demonstrate that robust quantization is possible if the pumped charge sector remains decoupled from hot spin excitations. This work provides crucial theoretical understanding regarding the limits of topological protection in strongly correlated materials under time-periodic driving.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamical robustness of quantized charge transport (Thouless pumping) when the system is initialized in highly entropic, spin-incoherent Mott states.
main_result: Quantized Thouless pumping can remain exponentially protected even in high-entropy Mott states due to dynamic decoupling from hot spin degrees of freedom. Conversely, other pump classes fail because spin excitations generate charge excitations.
method: The authors use analytical derivations, including mapping to spinless fermions and applying perturbation theory (Schrieffer-Wolff expansion) to derive effective low-energy Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system is based on the interacting Rice-Mele model Hamiltonian, analyzed in regimes ranging from non-interacting ($U=0$) to strongly correlated Mott insulators ($U=\infty$).
key_observables: Quantized charge transport per cycle (Delta Q), entropy, and heating rate of spin excitations.
important_parameters: Interaction strength U, driving frequency $\omega$, filling fraction (quarter-filling vs. half-filling).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes adiabatic driving with respect to the charge gap but explores regimes where spin dynamics are highly excited and incoherent.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate robust quantized transport at quarter-filling for large U, contrasting this with failure at half-filling due to spin gap closing. They also show time evolution of pumped charge under various protocols.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the standard Thouless pump, then introducing Mott-Thouless pumps in high-entropy regimes. It analytically proves protection mechanisms and contrasts these with failure modes caused by spin-charge coupling, supported by numerical simulations.
why_interesting: This work bridges topological physics (quantized pumping) with strongly correlated electron physics (Mott insulators), providing insights into how quantum coherence can be maintained in highly dissipative or thermally excited many-body systems.

During one pumping cycle, a unit charge is trans- ported by one unit cell, ∆x = 2a0. In the limit of strong repulsive interactions, the charge dynamics effectively decouples from the spin dynamics, so that quan- tized charge transport remains robust even in highly spin-incoherent states with large spin entropies.
